properties.description: For `process_deposit`, on success the shares minted must equal `amount` when vault.shares == vault.assets before the call and floor(amount * shares_before / assets_before) otherwise, with vault.shares increased by exactly that number and vault.assets increased by exactly `amount`; any other value means shares are mispriced against the vault's current share/asset ratio.
properties.title: deposit_mints_shares_at_current_ratio

properties.description: For both `process_deposit` and `process_deposit_exact`, the assets backing each pre-existing share must not decrease — assets_after * shares_before >= assets_before * shares_after — otherwise a depositor pays less than the fair backing for the shares they receive and silently extracts value from existing holders (note `process_deposit_exact` recomputes assets with the floor-rounding `convert_shares_to_assets` rather than `convert_shares_to_assets_ceil`).
properties.title: deposit_never_dilutes_existing_shareholders

properties.description: If vault.shares <= vault.assets holds before `process_deposit` or `process_deposit_exact`, it must still hold after the handler returns successfully; violating it means the vault records more outstanding shares than assets to back them and later redeemers cannot be paid.
properties.title: deposits_preserve_vault_solvency

properties.description: `process_deposit` must revert when `user_assets_account` is the same account as `vault_assets_account` (the guard is present but commented out, while `process_deposit_exact` enforces it): with a self-transfer the token CPI moves no tokens, yet vault.assets and vault.shares are both increased, so the caller mints shares backed by assets that never entered the vault.
properties.title: deposit_must_reject_self_transfer

properties.description: In `process_deposit` and `process_deposit_exact`, the asset amount requested in the SPL transfer CPI (source `user_assets_account`, destination `vault_assets_account`, authority = the signing `authority`) must equal the increase in vault.assets, and the amount in the `mint_to` CPI (mint = vault.shares_mint, destination `user_shares_account`) must equal the increase in vault.shares; a mismatch makes the vault's ledger diverge from the real token balances.
properties.title: deposit_cpi_amounts_match_recorded_state_deltas

properties.description: If, before `process_deposit` or `process_deposit_exact`, vault.assets + vault.fee_amount <= the `amount` field of the SPL token account data of `vault_assets_account`, the same relation must hold afterwards; breaking it means the vault credits itself assets it does not hold, which no later instruction can reconcile downward (update_reward only syncs upward).
properties.title: recorded_assets_remain_backed_by_token_balance

properties.description: `process_deposit_exact` must never transfer more asset tokens out of `user_assets_account` than the `amount` instruction argument (assets_to_vault <= amount), since the whole point of the exact variant is to take only what is needed to back the minted shares; taking more pulls unauthorized tokens from the depositor.
properties.title: exact_deposit_never_takes_more_than_requested

properties.description: `process_deposit` and `process_deposit_exact` must fail unless both the number of shares minted and the number of assets added to the vault are strictly positive, so that a caller can neither surrender assets for zero shares nor obtain shares without contributing assets.
properties.title: deposit_rejects_zero_share_or_zero_asset_move

properties.description: `process_deposit` and `process_deposit_exact` must leave every Vault field other than `shares` and `assets` byte-identical — admin, slash_admin, shares_mint, assets_mint, vault_assets_account, vault_shares_mint_bump, vault_assets_account_bump, fee_bps, fee_amount and fee_token_account — since the vault is written through a zero-copy bytemuck cast and a wrong write would silently reassign authorities or PDAs.
properties.title: deposit_leaves_vault_configuration_unchanged

properties.description: `process_deposit` and `process_deposit_exact` must reject a `vault_info` account whose owner is not the vault program (and whose data is not a valid, initialized Vault): `VaultInfo::try_from` only reinterprets the raw bytes with `bytemuck::from_bytes` and checks assets_mint != shares_mint, so an attacker can supply a look-alike account they control with an arbitrary shares/assets ratio and arbitrary recorded mint/token-account keys to drive share minting.
properties.title: deposit_must_reject_foreign_owned_vault_account

properties.description: `process_deposit` and `process_deposit_exact` must revert if the `authority` account is not a signer, since that account is used as the transfer authority over `user_assets_account`; without the check the program becomes a confused deputy that moves a third party's asset tokens.
properties.title: deposit_requires_authority_signature

properties.description: When vault.fee_bps != 0, the fee-free variants `process_deposit` and `process_deposit_exact` should not succeed (the `require!(fee.is_zero())` check exists but is commented out in `vault_deposit_assets`); otherwise any depositor can simply call the standard deposit instruction instead of the fee-charging one and the protocol never collects the configured fee.
properties.title: standard_deposit_must_not_bypass_configured_fee

properties.description: `process_deposit` must be able to complete successfully for a well-formed call — distinct `user_assets_account` and `vault_assets_account`, a signing `authority`, the correct vault-derived `vault_assets_account`/`shares_mint` PDAs, a solvent vault and an `amount` large enough to yield a nonzero share count — so that the accumulated guards do not render the deposit path dead.
properties.title: legitimate_deposit_is_reachable

properties.description: From a vault state where shares == 0 and assets > 0 (reachable by donating tokens plus `update_reward`, or by full redemption after reward accrual), `process_deposit` and `process_deposit_exact` compute floor(amount * 0 / assets) = 0 shares for every `amount` and then fail in `mint_shares`, permanently bricking deposits and leaving the residual assets unredeemable; a correct implementation should fall back to a 1:1 (or other well-defined) bootstrap ratio in that state.
properties.title: deposit_dead_when_shares_zero_but_assets_positive

properties.description: For `process_deposit` and `process_deposit_exact`, the assets taken from the depositor (the increase in vault.assets, equal to the amount in the SPL transfer CPI) must not exceed the pre-state value of the shares minted rounded up — assets_delta * shares_before <= shares_minted * assets_before when shares_before != assets_before (rounding the right-hand side up), and assets_delta <= shares_minted when shares_before == assets_before — otherwise the depositor surrenders assets that the shares they receive do not entitle them to reclaim, and that value is silently donated to pre-existing shareholders; this is exactly the inflation-attack loss the 'exact' variant is meant to remove, and `process_deposit` takes the full `amount` regardless of how far floor(amount * shares_before / assets_before) truncates.
properties.title: deposit_never_overcharges_depositor_for_shares

properties.description: If, before `process_deposit` or `process_deposit_exact`, vault.shares equals the `supply` field of the `shares_mint` account, the equality must still hold after the handler returns successfully (checking this requires a model of the SPL Token mint_to CPI, the same modelling assumption the assets-side backing property already makes; the bound here is a single mint account): if vault.shares falls below the circulating share supply the vault will not honour every outstanding share token and the last redeemers cannot be paid, and if it rises above the supply the vault reserves assets against shares nobody holds, stranding them permanently.
properties.title: vault_shares_equals_shares_mint_supply

properties.description: Spanning a sequence of two transactions: a `process_deposit` (or `process_deposit_exact`) that mints S shares and takes A assets, followed immediately by a `process_redeem_shares` of exactly those S shares on the same vault with no instruction in between, must return at most A assets to the user; if it can return more, the floor/ceil asymmetry between `convert_assets_to_shares` and `convert_shares_to_assets` lets anyone repeatedly cycle deposit-and-redeem to extract assets from the vault with no capital at risk, draining existing shareholders.
properties.title: deposit_then_redeem_is_not_profitable

properties.description: For `process_deposit` and `process_deposit_exact`, when the `vault_assets_account` SPL token account holds strictly more tokens than `vault.assets + vault.fee_amount` before the call (an accrued reward or plain donation that the permissionless `process_update_reward` has not yet recognized), the handler prices shares off the stale recorded `vault.assets` and mints floor(amount * shares / assets_recorded) shares instead of the fair floor(amount * shares / real_balance), handing the new depositor a pro-rata claim on the unrecognized tokens; the rule to check is that after either handler succeeds, token_balance_after * shares_before >= token_balance_before * shares_after, where token_balance is the `amount` field of the `vault_assets_account` token account, and a violation means existing shareholders' claim on the vault's real holdings is diluted by the incoming depositor (this reuses the SPL-token-account model that the existing backing property already assumes; the bound is one token account).
properties.title: deposit_prices_shares_against_stale_asset_balance

properties.description: In `process_deposit_with_fee`, the fee transferred to `vault_fee_account` must equal exactly floor(amount * vault.fee_bps / 10000) and the amount transferred to `vault_assets_account` must equal exactly amount - fee, so the two CPI amounts sum to exactly the caller-supplied `amount`; otherwise the depositor is over-charged or the protocol under-collects its fee.
properties.title: fee_is_exact_floor_bps_and_split_sums_to_amount

properties.description: Both `process_deposit_with_fee` and `process_deposit_with_fee_exact` must abort, leaving the Vault account byte-identical and performing no token transfer or mint, whenever the stored `vault.fee_bps` exceeds 10000, since a fee above 100% would otherwise produce a fee larger than the deposit and a nonsensical (underflowing) net amount.
properties.title: fee_bps_cap_enforced_before_any_effect

properties.description: For both `process_deposit_with_fee` and `process_deposit_with_fee_exact`, the increase in `vault.assets` must equal exactly the amount argument of the SPL Token transfer into `vault_assets_account` (the net, post-fee figure) and must not include the fee portion; if the handler moves assets into the vault token account without crediting `vault.assets` (or credits more than it moves), the vault's recorded asset total permanently diverges from the assets backing it.
properties.title: vault_assets_increase_equals_net_transferred_in

properties.description: For both `process_deposit_with_fee` and `process_deposit_with_fee_exact`, the increase in `vault.shares` must equal exactly the amount argument of the `mint_to` CPI that mints shares to `user_shares_account`; minting shares to a user without incrementing `vault.shares` makes the circulating share supply exceed the vault's accounting, corrupting the redemption ratio and making later redemptions underflow.
properties.title: vault_shares_increase_equals_shares_minted

properties.description: If `vault.shares <= vault.assets` holds before `process_deposit_with_fee` or `process_deposit_with_fee_exact` runs, it must still hold after the handler returns successfully; a violation means the vault owes more shares than it has assets to back and some redeemer cannot be paid.
properties.title: fee_deposit_preserves_solvency

properties.description: For both fee-deposit handlers, the post-state must satisfy assets_after * shares_before >= assets_before * shares_after (evaluated over exact integers), i.e. the depositor must never receive shares worth more assets at the pre-deposit ratio than the net amount they contributed, otherwise a depositor extracts value from existing share holders.
properties.title: fee_deposit_does_not_dilute_existing_holders

properties.description: Neither `process_deposit_with_fee` nor `process_deposit_with_fee_exact` may modify `vault.fee_amount`, because their fee is delivered to the separate `vault_fee_account` token account and is therefore not backed by any balance in `vault_assets_account`; incrementing the counter would let the Fee Collection instruction withdraw depositor-backing assets out of the vault's asset account.
properties.title: fee_deposit_leaves_fee_amount_counter_unchanged

properties.description: Both fee-deposit handlers must leave `vault.admin`, `vault.slash_admin`, `vault.assets_mint`, `vault.shares_mint`, `vault.fee_token_account`, `vault.vault_assets_account`, `vault.fee_bps`, `vault.vault_shares_mint_bump` and `vault.vault_assets_account_bump` bit-identical, since a deposit that rewrites any configuration field of the zero-copy Vault struct would hand over admin control or redirect future transfers.
properties.title: fee_deposit_leaves_vault_configuration_fields_unchanged

properties.description: Both fee-deposit handlers must fail whenever the passed `vault_assets_account` and `user_assets_account` are the same account, because an SPL self-transfer moves no tokens while the handler would still credit `vault.assets` and mint shares, letting a depositor mint shares backed by assets that never arrived.
properties.title: fee_deposit_rejects_vault_user_asset_account_aliasing

properties.description: `VaultInfo::try_from` deserializes the Vault with bytemuck without checking that the account's owner is this program (and without any discriminator check), so both fee-deposit handlers must reject a `vault_info` account not owned by the vault program; otherwise an attacker supplies a fabricated Vault whose `vault_assets_account`, `fee_token_account`, `assets_mint`, `shares_mint` and bump fields they control, making every 'must equal vault.X' constraint in `DepositWithFeeContext::validate` vacuous — and the exact variant never writes the account, so the runtime's ownership check on data mutation does not catch it either.
properties.title: vault_info_owner_and_discriminator_unchecked

properties.description: Unlike `DepositContext`, `DepositWithFeeContext` never re-derives the vault's PDAs, so both fee-deposit handlers must additionally verify that `vault_assets_account` equals the program address for seeds [VAULT_ASSETS, vault_info.key, vault.vault_assets_account_bump] and that `shares_mint` equals the program address for seeds [SHARES_MINT, vault_info.key, vault.vault_shares_mint_bump]; without this the `mint_to` CPI is signed with a bump read out of unverified vault state and a substituted asset account or mint can receive the deposit or issue the shares.
properties.title: fee_deposit_does_not_rederive_vault_pdas

properties.description: Neither fee-deposit handler may debit the depositor (net transfer or fee transfer with a non-zero amount) unless the number of shares minted to `user_shares_account` is strictly positive, and it may not mint shares when no assets are transferred into the vault; the `exact` variant bypasses the `amt > 0` guards inside `Vault::mint_shares`/`Vault::add_token`, so a deposit that rounds to zero shares could still take the user's tokens.
properties.title: no_user_assets_debited_without_positive_shares

properties.description: In `process_deposit_with_fee_exact`, the amount transferred into `vault_assets_account` must equal exactly the assets needed to back the shares minted at the pre-deposit ratio (convert_shares_to_assets(shares_minted)) and the sum of that transfer and the fee transfer must not exceed the caller-supplied `amount`; otherwise the handler collects assets the depositor receives no shares for, which is precisely the inflation-attack leak this variant exists to prevent.
properties.title: exact_fee_deposit_never_over_collects_assets

properties.description: There must exist an execution of `process_deposit_with_fee` with a solvent vault, `vault.fee_bps` strictly below 10000, correctly matched vault-derived accounts, a signing authority and an `amount` large enough to buy at least one share, in which the handler returns success and mints a positive number of shares — confirming the guard stack has not made the fee-deposit path dead.
properties.title: legitimate_fee_deposit_is_reachable

properties.description: Both fee-deposit handlers must remain usable when the vault has no outstanding shares: for any vault with vault.shares == 0 and vault.fee_bps < 10000 there must exist an `amount` for which `process_deposit_with_fee` succeeds and mints a strictly positive number of shares, regardless of how large vault.assets is — today `convert_assets_to_shares` returns floor(net * 0 / assets) = 0 once vault.assets > 0 while vault.shares == 0, so `process_deposit_with_fee` always fails the `require_gt!(amt, 0)` guard in `Vault::mint_shares` and `process_deposit_with_fee_exact` always fails with MathOverflow when `convert_shares_to_assets(0)` divides by num_shares() == 0, meaning an attacker who transfers one asset token to the vault's asset PDA and calls the permissionless `process_update_reward` permanently kills all deposits into that vault and strands the donated assets (no shares exist that could be burned to recover them).
properties.title: fee_deposit_bricked_when_share_supply_is_zero

properties.description: Started from the same Vault pre-state with the same `amount`, `process_deposit_with_fee_exact` must mint exactly the same number of shares to `user_shares_account` as `process_deposit_with_fee` would, and the total debited from `user_assets_account` (net transfer plus fee transfer) must be no greater than the total the plain variant debits, so the over-collection protection is never paid for by the depositor; if the exact variant mints fewer shares or debits more assets for the same request, depositors are silently worse off on the path they are told is safer (a relational rule that invokes both handlers/operations on two copies of one arbitrary vault state).
properties.title: exact_fee_deposit_is_a_refinement_of_plain_fee_deposit

properties.description: Spanning a two-instruction sequence: if `process_deposit_with_fee` or `process_deposit_with_fee_exact` succeeds and mints s > 0 shares while debiting n assets into `vault_assets_account`, then an immediately following `process_redeem_shares(s)` by the same user against the same vault must succeed and must pay out at most n assets — failure of the first half means the depositor's assets are permanently stranded (the exact variant never increments `vault.shares`, so `burn_shares(s)` underflows and the position can never be unwound), and failure of the second half means deposit/redeem round-tripping extracts assets belonging to other share holders.
properties.title: fee_deposit_shares_are_redeemable_without_profit

properties.description: For both `process_deposit_with_fee` and `process_deposit_with_fee_exact`, the number of shares passed to the `mint_to` CPI must be at least the pre-deposit conversion of the assets actually transferred into `vault_assets_account` (i.e. at least `t` when vault.shares == vault.assets before the call, otherwise at least floor(t * vault.shares_before / vault.assets_before), where t is the amount argument of the transfer into `vault_assets_account`); if the handler mints fewer shares than the net assets it debits are worth, the depositor's assets are silently confiscated and redistributed to existing share holders.
properties.title: depositor_receives_full_value_for_net_deposit

properties.description: In `process_deposit_with_fee_exact`, the amount argument of the SPL Token transfer to `vault_fee_account` must never exceed floor(amount * vault.fee_bps / 10000), the maximum fee implied by the caller's requested `amount` and the vault's advertised rate; since this variant applies the basis-point rate a second time to a recomputed figure, a wrong basis would overcharge the depositor beyond the advertised fee while still keeping the two transfers' sum within `amount`.
properties.title: exact_fee_never_exceeds_consented_bps_of_requested_amount

properties.description: process_collect_fee may succeed only if the passed `authority` account is a signer and its key equals the `admin` field stored in the vault account at entry; on any other authority it must revert leaving vault.fee_amount unchanged and issuing no token transfer, otherwise anyone can drain the vault's accumulated fees.
properties.title: admin_signer_required_for_collect_fee

properties.description: On a successful process_collect_fee the program issues exactly one SPL-Token transfer whose amount equals the vault.fee_amount value read at entry, whose source is vault.vault_assets_account, whose destination is the passed fee_collect_account, and which is signed with the vault-assets PDA seeds; transferring more would let the admin take assets that back depositor shares, transferring less would zero the fee while paying out nothing.
properties.title: collect_fee_transfers_exactly_recorded_fee

properties.description: After a successful process_collect_fee the vault's fee_amount field is exactly zero, so a second call in the same or a later transaction pays out nothing; if the field were left non-zero the admin could replay the claim and repeatedly drain the vault asset token account.
properties.title: collect_fee_zeroes_fee_amount

properties.description: process_collect_fee leaves vault.assets and vault.shares unchanged (fees are accounted separately from share-backing assets), so the solvency relation shares <= assets is preserved and no share holder is diluted or under-backed by a fee claim.
properties.title: collect_fee_preserves_assets_and_shares

properties.description: No instruction handler in the program (process_deposit, process_deposit_exact, process_deposit_with_fee, process_deposit_with_fee_exact, process_redeem_shares, process_update_reward, process_slash, process_collect_fee) modifies vault.admin, vault.slash_admin, vault.assets_mint, vault.shares_mint, vault.fee_token_account, vault.vault_assets_account, vault.fee_bps, vault.vault_assets_account_bump or vault.vault_shares_mint_bump — otherwise fee-collection authority or the vault's token/mint bindings could be hijacked through an unrelated instruction.
properties.title: vault_config_fields_immutable

properties.description: vault.fee_amount is never decreased by any handler other than process_collect_fee (checked across process_deposit, process_deposit_exact, process_deposit_with_fee, process_deposit_with_fee_exact, process_redeem_shares, process_update_reward, process_slash), and process_collect_fee decreases it exactly to zero; any other decrease silently destroys accrued protocol fees.
properties.title: fee_amount_only_cleared_by_collect_fee

properties.description: Starting from a state in which the vault asset token account balance covers the recorded assets but not the recorded fee (balance >= vault.assets and balance < vault.assets + vault.fee_amount — reachable because process_update_reward syncs vault.assets to the raw token-account balance, which already includes the accrued fee), process_collect_fee pays out fee_amount without ever reading the token balance and leaves the account holding less than vault.assets, so later redemptions of legitimate shares fail; the handler should bound the payout by balance - vault.assets.
properties.title: collect_fee_must_not_spend_share_backing_assets

properties.description: process_collect_fee must reject any vault_info account whose owner is not the certora_vault program, because VaultInfo::try_from deserializes the account with bytemuck and checks no owner and no discriminator, so a look-alike account whose `admin` is the attacker and whose fee_amount/bump are attacker-chosen is accepted as authoritative vault state.
properties.title: collect_fee_requires_program_owned_vault

properties.description: process_collect_fee must re-derive the vault assets account as PDA(VAULT_ASSETS, vault_info.key, vault.vault_assets_account_bump) and require the passed vault_assets_account to equal it (the check DepositContext and SlashContext perform but CollectFeeContext omits), since the handler signs the transfer with exactly those seeds; without the re-derivation the transfer source and the PDA authority used to sign are not tied together and a non-canonical bump or a mis-recorded vault_assets_account is accepted.
properties.title: collect_fee_requires_derived_vault_assets_pda

properties.description: process_collect_fee must reject a fee_collect_account equal to vault_assets_account; otherwise the CPI is a self-transfer that moves nothing while vault.fee_amount is zeroed, destroying the fee claim and leaving the assets to be re-classified as depositor reward by process_update_reward (the analogous SelfTransfer guard exists in process_deposit_with_fee).
properties.title: collect_fee_rejects_self_transfer

properties.description: There exists an execution of process_collect_fee in which the recorded admin signs, the vault is program-owned and internally consistent, the vault assets account is the correctly derived PDA and fee_amount > 0, and the instruction succeeds — confirming the account checks do not make fee collection unreachable (dead handler / permanently stuck fees).
properties.title: collect_fee_reachable_for_admin

properties.description: If vault.shares <= vault.assets holds before process_redeem_shares, it must still hold after a successful call, so the vault can never end a redemption owing more shares than it records assets to back them.
properties.title: redeem_preserves_solvency

properties.description: On a successful process_redeem_shares(amount), vault.assets decreases by exactly `amount` when the pre-state shares equal the pre-state assets, and otherwise by exactly floor(amount * assets_before / shares_before) computed from the pre-redemption totals; any other payout over- or under-pays the redeemer at the expense of the remaining share holders.
properties.title: redeem_payout_equals_floor_of_pre_ratio

properties.description: On a successful process_redeem_shares(amount), vault.shares decreases by exactly `amount`, the amount passed to the SPL Token burn CPI equals `amount`, and the amount passed to the SPL Token transfer CPI equals the decrease in vault.assets; a mismatch makes the recorded vault accounting diverge from the tokens actually moved.
properties.title: redeem_burns_exactly_requested_shares_and_cpi_amounts_match

properties.description: A successful process_redeem_shares must satisfy assets_after * shares_before >= assets_before * shares_after, i.e. the per-share asset backing never decreases across a redemption, so rounding in the share-to-asset conversion always favors the vault rather than the redeemer.
properties.title: redeem_does_not_dilute_remaining_holders

properties.description: process_redeem_shares must reject (rather than wrap or truncate) any request where `amount` exceeds the vault's recorded shares or where the computed payout exceeds the vault's recorded assets, so neither vault.shares nor vault.assets can underflow into a huge value that would let the vault be drained by a subsequent redemption.
properties.title: redeem_rejects_over_redemption_without_wrapping

properties.description: A successful process_redeem_shares implies the `authority` account is a signer; if the signer check were dropped, anyone could burn another user's shares and route the asset payout to their own token account.
properties.title: redeem_requires_authority_signature

properties.description: A successful process_redeem_shares implies vault_info.owner equals the certora_vault program id; VaultInfo deserializes the account with bytemuck without any owner or discriminant check, so a look-alike account created under another program would let an attacker dictate shares, assets, the recorded vault_assets_account and the PDA bumps used to sign the asset transfer.
properties.title: redeem_requires_vault_info_owned_by_program

properties.description: A successful process_redeem_shares implies vault_assets_account.key equals the address derived from seeds [VAULT_ASSETS, vault_info.key, vault.vault_assets_account_bump] under the program id — the very seeds the handler uses in invoke_signed; RedeemSharesContext::validate only compares the key to the unverified vault.vault_assets_account field and never calls check_vault (unlike DepositContext and SlashContext), so the program can be made to sign a transfer out of an account that is not its canonical assets PDA.
properties.title: redeem_vault_assets_account_must_be_canonical_pda

properties.description: A successful process_redeem_shares implies shares_mint.key equals both vault.shares_mint and the address derived from seeds [SHARES_MINT, vault_info.key, vault.vault_shares_mint_bump]; the redeem context never re-derives the shares mint PDA, so a spoofed or mis-recorded mint would make the burn CPI destroy tokens of a mint unrelated to the vault's shares while still crediting the redeemer with vault assets.
properties.title: redeem_shares_mint_must_be_canonical_pda

properties.description: process_redeem_shares must fail when vault_assets_account.key equals user_assets_account.key; otherwise shares are burned and vault.assets is decremented while no tokens actually leave the vault token account, and a subsequent permissionless update_reward re-credits those assets, inflating the share price for the attacker's remaining shares.
properties.title: redeem_rejects_vault_to_self_transfer

properties.description: Both cross-program invocations issued by process_redeem_shares (the shares burn and the asset transfer) must target the canonical SPL Token program id; if the program id were taken from an unvalidated account, an attacker could point it at malicious code while the vault's PDA signs the transfer instruction.
properties.title: redeem_cpis_only_to_canonical_spl_token_program

properties.description: A successful process_redeem_shares must leave vault.admin, vault.slash_admin, vault.shares_mint, vault.assets_mint, vault.vault_assets_account, vault.vault_shares_mint_bump, vault.vault_assets_account_bump, vault.fee_bps and vault.fee_amount byte-identical to their pre-call values; a redemption that mutates any of these could hijack the vault's admin or fee accounting.
properties.title: redeem_leaves_vault_config_unchanged

properties.description: For a solvent vault (shares <= assets), a signing authority, correctly derived accounts and 0 < amount <= vault.shares, process_redeem_shares must succeed — the post-decrement solvency re-check inside del_token must never make an otherwise legitimate redemption impossible, which would strand user funds.
properties.title: redeem_reachable_for_legitimate_user

properties.description: Spanning a sequence of two instructions: if a user deposits X assets and receives S shares, an immediately following process_redeem_shares(S) by that user must pay out at most X assets, so no round trip through the vault extracts value from existing share holders.
properties.title: deposit_then_redeem_round_trip_no_profit

properties.description: After a successful process_redeem_shares, if vault.shares is 0 then vault.assets must also be 0 — a redemption must never leave the vault with zero outstanding shares but a non-zero recorded asset balance, because such a vault is permanently bricked (further deposits abort since convert_assets_to_shares yields 0 and mint_shares requires a positive amount, and further redemptions abort on division by zero shares), stranding the residual assets forever.
properties.title: redeem_never_leaves_shareless_vault_with_assets

properties.description: `process_update_reward` performs no cross-program invocation and writes to no account other than the Vault state account — in particular the data (balance) of `vault_assets_account` and the lamports of every passed account are unchanged — since recognizing a reward is a pure bookkeeping sync.

properties.description: Given a program-owned Vault account, its canonical asset token PDA holding a balance strictly greater than `vault.assets`, and no signer among the passed accounts, `process_update_reward` succeeds and increases `vault.assets` by exactly (balance - old assets), confirming the intended permissionless reward path is not dead.
properties.title: update_reward_reachable_without_any_signer

properties.description: On a successful process_slash, the vault's recorded assets decrease by exactly the `amount` argument (vault.assets_after == vault.assets_before - amount computed over exact integers, never wrapping) and the amount handed to the SPL Token transfer CPI equals exactly that same `amount`, so recorded assets can never diverge from the tokens actually moved out.

properties.description: If vault.shares <= vault.assets holds before the call, then after any successful process_slash vault.shares <= vault.assets still holds; equivalently process_slash must reject every `amount` greater than vault.assets - vault.shares (and every `amount` greater than vault.assets, with no underflow of the assets counter), since otherwise outstanding shares would no longer be fully backed and redeemers could not be paid. properties.title: slash_preserves_vault_solvency

properties.description: A successful process_slash must leave every Vault field other than `assets` byte-identical to its pre-state value — in particular shares, admin, slash_admin, shares_mint, assets_mint, fee_bps, fee_amount, fee_token_account, vault_assets_account, vault_assets_account_bump and vault_shares_mint_bump — so that the slash admin cannot use this instruction to escalate to vault admin, zero or inflate the fee counter, or re-point the vault's PDAs.
properties.title: slash_modifies_only_assets_field

properties.description: vault_info is deserialized with bytemuck from a raw AccountInfo whose `owner` is never compared to the certora_vault program id (VaultInfo::validate only checks assets_mint != shares_mint), so process_slash must be shown to reject any vault_info account not owned by this program; otherwise an attacker supplies a look-alike account they created under another program with slash_admin set to their own key and passes the authority check.

properties.description: A well-formed slash must actually be executable: with vault_info owned by the program and internally consistent, vault_assets_account equal to the recorded/derived assets PDA, the canonical SPL Token program passed, the signing authority equal to vault.slash_admin, and 0 < amount <= vault.assets - vault.shares, process_slash must succeed rather than revert, ensuring the guards are not so strict that the slashing path is unreachable.

groups.title: Deposit share pricing matches current vault ratio
groups.description: Standard and fee-based deposits must mint shares that exactly reflect the pre-deposit share-to-asset ratio (or 1:1 when the vault is empty), with no rounding or logic error letting a depositor take more value than contributed or receive fewer shares than owed.

groups.title: Exact-amount deposit variants never over-collect assets
groups.description: The exact-amount deposit handlers must transfer no more than the assets actually needed to back the shares minted, must never take more than the requested amount, and must correctly apply the configured fee rate without double-charging.

groups.title: Deposits reject zero-share or zero-asset transfers
groups.description: Deposit handlers must fail rather than let a caller mint shares without contributing assets or transfer assets without receiving any shares in return.

groups.title: Deposits preserve solvency and accurate vault bookkeeping
groups.description: Across standard and fee-based deposit paths, the vault's recorded shares must never exceed its recorded assets, and the CPI token-transfer and mint amounts must exactly match the changes recorded in vault state, including the share-mint supply tracking.

groups.title: Deposits never alter vault configuration or authority fields
groups.description: Deposit handlers (standard and fee-based) must leave every Vault field unrelated to assets and shares byte-identical, preventing a deposit call from silently reassigning admin authority, mints, PDAs, or fee settings.

groups.title: Deposits reject forged or misrouted accounts
groups.description: Deposit handlers must reject self-transfers, vault_info accounts not owned by the program, and vault asset/mint accounts that are not the canonically derived PDAs, preventing an attacker from supplying forged state or routing funds through unauthorized accounts.

groups.title: Fee-based deposit paths charge the exact configured fee
groups.description: The fee-based deposit handlers must compute the protocol fee as the exact floor of the configured basis-point rate, split the transfer so it sums to the requested amount, and standard fee-free deposits must not be usable as a bypass when a fee is configured.

groups.title: Legitimate deposits remain executable, including edge cases
groups.description: Well-formed deposit calls must be able to succeed for both standard and fee-based paths, and the vault must not become permanently stuck in a zero-share, positive-asset state that bricks all future deposits.

groups.title: Depositing and immediately redeeming cannot extract value
groups.description: A deposit immediately followed by a redemption of the resulting shares must never pay out more assets than were originally deposited, closing off a no-risk arbitrage loop against other shareholders; this holds for both standard and fee-based deposit paths.

groups.title: Deposit pricing reflects real token balance, not stale state
groups.description: If the vault's actual token balance exceeds its recorded assets due to an unrecognized donation or reward, deposits must not let the new depositor claim a pro-rata share of the unrecognized surplus at existing shareholders' expense.

groups.title: Fee collection pays exactly the recorded fee to the admin
groups.description: Only the recorded admin, as a signer, may collect protocol fees, and a successful collection must transfer exactly the recorded fee amount to the designated fee account, zero the fee counter afterward, and leave vault assets and shares untouched.

groups.title: Fee collection rejects forged, misrouted, or self-transfer accounts
groups.description: Fee collection must only operate on a program-owned vault, must re-derive and check the canonical vault-assets PDA before signing the transfer, must reject a destination identical to the source account, and must never pay out more than the token balance actually backing depositor shares.

groups.title: Core vault configuration and fee accounting change only through authorized paths
groups.description: Across every instruction handler in the program, the vault's administrative, mint, PDA-bump, and fee-rate fields must never be mutated, and the accrued fee counter may only ever be decreased to zero by the dedicated fee-collection instruction.

groups.title: Redemption preserves solvency and matches recorded token movements
groups.description: A successful redemption must keep outstanding shares fully backed by assets, decrease vault shares and assets by exactly the requested amount and its fair-value payout, and ensure the burn and transfer CPI amounts match these recorded deltas with no dilution of remaining holders.

groups.title: Redemption rejects forged accounts, bad signers, and wrong CPI targets
groups.description: Redemption must require a genuine authority signature, a program-owned vault, canonical PDA derivation for both the vault assets account and the shares mint, distinct asset and share mints, calls only to the real SPL Token program, and must reject a self-transfer that would burn shares without moving assets.

groups.title: Redemption leaves configuration untouched and remains usable
groups.description: A successful redemption must not alter any vault configuration field, must be reachable for a legitimate solvent request, and must never leave the vault with outstanding assets but zero shares, which would strand those assets permanently.

groups.title: Reward sync exactly tracks token balance without diluting holders
groups.description: The permissionless reward-update instruction must set recorded assets to exactly the real token balance, reject balances below the currently recorded assets, never decrease assets or alter shares, and preserve the vault's solvency invariant throughout.

groups.title: Reward sync performs no transfers and touches no configuration
groups.description: The reward-update instruction must be a pure state write that performs no cross-program invocation, moves no value, and leaves every vault configuration field untouched.

groups.title: Reward sync validates accounts and avoids bricking the vault
groups.description: The reward-update instruction must require a program-owned vault and a canonically derived, correctly-owned token account before trusting its balance, must not count pending uncollected fees as recognized reward, must not create stranded assets when no shares exist, and must remain reachable without requiring any signer.

groups.title: Slashing is admin-gated and reduces assets by an exact, solvent amount
groups.description: Only the recorded slash admin, as a signer, may invoke slashing, and a successful slash must decrease recorded assets by exactly the requested amount, match that amount in the token transfer CPI, preserve the vault's solvency invariant, and touch no other vault field.

groups.title: Slashing rejects forged vault, asset, and mint accounts
groups.description: Slashing must reject a vault account not owned by the program, must bind the asset account to the vault's recorded pubkey as well as its PDA derivation, must sign solely with validated vault-derived seeds, and should bind the asset mint to the vault's recorded mint to prevent operating on an unrelated token.

groups.title: Legitimate slashing remains executable
groups.description: A well-formed slash request by the recorded slash admin against a correctly-derived, solvent vault must succeed rather than being blocked by overly strict guards, ensuring the slashing path is not dead.

findings.title: Missing empty-share-supply bootstrap in convert_assets_to_shares permanently bricks all deposits once a vault reaches shares == 0 with assets > 0

content.summary: `Vault::convert_assets_to_shares` has no special case for an empty share supply: when `vault.shares == 0` and `vault.assets > 0` it computes `mul_div_floor(net_amount, 0, assets) == 0` for every possible deposit amount, so `mint_shares(0)` always trips `require_gt!(amt, 0)`. The Certora satisfy rule `rule_fee_deposit_bricked_when_share_supply_is_zero` was refuted — no deposit amount at all can mint shares on such a vault — and the state is permissionlessly reachable by donating one asset token and calling `process_update_reward`, after which deposits are dead forever and the donated assets are unrecoverable because no shares exist to burn.
content.description:
The rule `rule_fee_deposit_bricked_when_share_supply_is_zero` is an existential (`cvlr_satisfy!`) property: for an otherwise unconstrained `Vault` with `v.shares == 0`, `v.num_assets() > 0` and `u64::from(v.fee_bps) < 10000`, it asks the Prover to exhibit *any* `amount: u64` for which `crate::operations::vault_deposit_assets_with_fee(&mut v, amount)` succeeds and yields `shares_to_user > 0`. The Prover returned no witness, which for a satisfy rule is the refutation itself: over the entire `u64` range of deposit amounts, no execution mints a positive number of shares.

The causal chain is fully contained in the accounting core — the rule drives a pure `&mut Vault` transition with no accounts, no `Context`, no CPI, no PDA derivation, and no mocked or havoced symbol on the path, so the defect cannot be attributed to harness plumbing:

1. `vault_deposit_assets_with_fee` (`programs/vault/src/operations/vault_fee_operations.rs`) calls `vault.fee_in_bps()`, which succeeds because `FeeBps::try_from` only rejects values above `10000`. It then computes `net_amount = amount - floor(amount * fee_bps / 10000)`, which is well defined and ranges over essentially all of `u64`.
2. `Vault::convert_assets_to_shares` (`programs/vault/src/state.rs`) special-cases only `num_shares() == num_assets()`. With `shares == 0` and `assets > 0` that shortcut is not taken, so control falls through to `mul_div_floor(net_amount, num_shares(), num_assets()) = floor(net_amount * 0 / assets) = 0`. Multiplication by a zero share supply annihilates the operand, making the result a function of the pre-state alone — quantifying over every `amount` buys nothing.
3. `vault.mint_shares(0)` hits `require_gt!(amt, 0, VaultError::GuardFail)` and returns `Err`.

Both conjuncts are therefore jointly unreachable: `ok` is always false and `shares_to_user` is always `0`. The vault fields the rule left free (`admin`, mints, bumps, `fee_amount`) are never read on this path and so cannot be what blocks the witness.

The symmetric gap exists on the other side of the conversion: `convert_shares_to_assets` and `convert_shares_to_assets_ceil` divide by `num_shares()`, so on the same `shares == 0` state they return `MathOverflow`. This makes `process_deposit_with_fee_exact` fail as well, and it means no redemption-style path can be used to extract the stranded assets either. (This second half follows from reading the source — the refuted rule only drives `vault_deposit_assets_with_fee` — but it is a direct consequence of the same missing bootstrap case.)

Crucially, the bricking state is not merely hypothetical: it is permissionlessly reachable. An attacker transfers a single asset token into the vault's asset PDA and invokes the permissionless `process_update_reward`, whose `vault_update_reward` calls `add_token(reward)` and increases `assets` without minting any shares. On a fresh or fully-exited vault (`shares == 0`), this moves the vault into `shares == 0 && assets > 0` — the exact pre-state the Prover proved admits no successful deposit.

The remediation is to add an empty-share-supply bootstrap to the conversion arithmetic: when `num_shares() == 0`, a deposit should mint shares one-for-one against the net assets contributed rather than computing `floor(token * 0 / assets)`, and `convert_shares_to_assets`/`convert_shares_to_assets_ceil` need a consistent empty-supply case so they do not divide by zero. Because a plain one-for-one bootstrap hands any previously donated assets to the first depositor (the classic inflation-attack surface), it should be paired with a virtual-shares/virtual-assets offset applied inside both conversions, or a minimum initial deposit whose shares are minted to the program. Separately, it is worth gating `process_update_reward` on a vault with no outstanding shares, since in that configuration there is no holder for the reward to accrue to.
content.impact: Permanent denial of service on the vault plus permanently frozen assets. Once a vault is in `shares == 0 && assets > 0`, every deposit through `process_deposit_with_fee` fails the `require_gt!(amt, 0)` guard in `mint_shares` for every possible amount, and `process_deposit_with_fee_exact` fails with `MathOverflow` because `convert_shares_to_assets` divides by a zero share supply. The vault can never again accept a deposit, and since no shares exist, there is nothing to burn to withdraw the assets sitting in the asset account — the donated/accrued assets are stranded with no recovery path. An attacker can inflict this on a fresh or fully-exited vault for the cost of a single asset token and one permissionless instruction call.
content.attack_path:
1. Identify a vault with `shares == 0` — i.e. any newly initialized vault before its first deposit, or one from which all shares have been redeemed.
2. Transfer a single asset token into the vault's asset PDA token account.
3. Call the permissionless `process_update_reward` instruction. Its `vault_update_reward` invokes `add_token(reward)`, raising `vault.assets` above zero without minting any shares.
4. The vault is now in `shares == 0 && assets > 0`. Any subsequent `process_deposit_with_fee` call computes `net_amount = amount - fee`, then `convert_assets_to_shares(net_amount) = mul_div_floor(net_amount, 0, assets) = 0`, and `mint_shares(0)` reverts on `require_gt!(amt, 0, VaultError::GuardFail)` — for every amount, as the refuted satisfy rule proves.
5. `process_deposit_with_fee_exact` is dead on the same state because `convert_shares_to_assets(0)` divides by `num_shares() == 0` and returns `MathOverflow`.
6. No shares exist, so no redemption can move the donated assets out. The vault is permanently unusable and the assets are permanently stranded.
content.assumptions_and_uncertainties: The refutation is direct evidence only for `vault_deposit_assets_with_fee`, the accounting core of `process_deposit_with_fee`; the rule never calls `vault_deposit_assets_with_fee_exact` and never exercises handler-level account plumbing. The claim that the `_exact` variant is likewise dead on this state (via `convert_shares_to_assets` dividing by `num_shares() == 0`) is derived from reading `programs/vault/src/state.rs`, not from this Prover run. Likewise, the reachability step via donating one asset token plus a permissionless `process_update_reward` / `vault_update_reward` → `add_token(reward)` is taken from source reading rather than being produced by this rule, which starts from a `nondet_vault()` pre-state; it assumes `process_update_reward` is in fact callable by an unprivileged signer and does not itself reject vaults with zero outstanding shares. If some other instruction or initialization invariant prevents a vault from ever holding assets while `shares == 0`, the likelihood drops, but the arithmetic defect in the conversion functions remains.

provenance.risk_reasoning: The Prover exhaustively refuted the existential over all `u64` deposit amounts, proving the deposit path is dead — not merely hard to use — on any vault with zero shares and positive assets, and the stranded assets are unrecoverable because no shares exist to burn. Reaching that state requires no privilege: any actor can transfer one asset token to the vault's asset PDA and call the permissionless `process_update_reward`, which increases `assets` via `add_token` without minting shares. The only precondition is a vault at `shares == 0`, which is the natural state of every newly created or fully-exited vault.

findings.title: Missing empty-share-supply bootstrap in share conversion permanently bricks all deposits on a vault with shares == 0 and assets > 0

content.summary: `Vault::convert_assets_to_shares` has no special case for an empty share supply: when `num_shares() == 0` and `num_assets() > 0` it falls through to `mul_div_floor(net, 0, assets)` and returns 0 shares for any deposit size. The Prover refuted the liveness property that some `amount` makes `process_deposit_with_fee` mint positive shares — every deposit fails at `mint_shares`'s `require_gt!(amt, 0)` guard. Since anyone can push a fresh vault into the `shares == 0 && assets > 0` state permissionlessly (donate one asset token, call `process_update_reward`), an attacker can permanently brick all deposits and strand the donated assets.
content.description:
The rule `rule_fee_deposit_bricked_when_share_supply_is_zero_witness` builds an unconstrained `Vault`, forces `v.shares = 0`, and assumes only three things inside the property's stated domain: `v.num_assets() > 0`, `u64::from(v.fee_bps) < 10000`, and `amount > 0`. It then drives the program's own accounting core `crate::operations::vault_deposit_assets_with_fee(&mut v, amount)` and asserts `ok && e.shares_to_user > 0`.

The counterexample (programs/vault/src/certora/specs/fee_based_deposits.rs:771) shows `a0 = v.num_assets() = 2^64 - 1`, `v.shares = 0`, `fb = v.fee_bps = 9999` (a legal rate strictly below the 10000 cap), and `amount = 2^64 - 1` — the largest expressible deposit, so the failure cannot be blamed on a too-small request. The logged effect is `s = 0, a = 0, f = 0` with `o = ok as u64 = 0`: the call returned `Err` and the zeros are `unwrap_or_default()` filler, not computed amounts. The assertion fails on its first conjunct.

The causal chain is fully visible in the source:

1. `vault_deposit_assets_with_fee` (`programs/vault/src/operations/vault_fee_operations.rs`) calls `vault.fee_in_bps()?`, which succeeds because `FeeBps::try_from`'s `require_le!` accepts 9999. It computes `net_amount = amount - floor(amount * 9999 / 10000)`, a strictly positive net.
2. It calls `vault.convert_assets_to_shares(net_amount)`. In `Vault::convert_assets_to_shares` (`programs/vault/src/state.rs`) the only shortcut is `num_shares() == num_assets()`, which does not apply (`0 != 2^64 - 1`). Control falls through to `mul_div_floor(net_amount, self.num_shares(), self.num_assets())` = `floor(net_amount * 0 / assets)`, which is 0 for every possible `net_amount` — multiplying by a zero share supply annihilates the operand.
3. `vault.mint_shares(0)` then trips `require_gt!(amt, 0, VaultError::GuardFail)` and returns `Err`.

Because `shares_to_user` is a function of the pre-state alone once `num_shares() == 0`, no choice of `amount` escapes: the fee-deposit path is not merely hard to hit on this state, it is unreachable. The rule drives a pure `&mut Vault` transition with no accounts, CPI, PDA derivation, or summarized symbols on the path, so the result is not an account-model or havoc artifact — every logged value is reproducible by hand from the two functions.

By source inspection (not exercised by this trace), the same pre-state also kills the `_exact` variant: `convert_shares_to_assets` / `convert_shares_to_assets_ceil` compute `mul_div_floor(shares, assets, num_shares())`, which divides by zero and yields `MathOverflow` when `num_shares() == 0`. Fixing only the assets-to-shares direction would leave that second route broken.

The `shares == 0 && assets > 0` configuration is reachable permissionlessly: `vault_update_reward` calls `add_token(reward)` and mints no shares against it, so anyone can transfer a single asset token into the vault's asset PDA and invoke the permissionless `process_update_reward` on a fresh vault. After that, every `process_deposit_with_fee` fails at `mint_shares(0)`, and because no shares exist, no one can burn shares to withdraw the donated assets.

Remediation belongs in `Vault::convert_assets_to_shares` and `convert_shares_to_assets`/`convert_shares_to_assets_ceil`: add an empty-supply case so a deposit into a zero-share vault mints shares against the net assets contributed instead of `floor(token * 0 / assets)`, and handle `num_shares() == 0` in the reverse direction so it does not divide by zero. Note that a naive one-for-one bootstrap hands any previously donated assets to the first depositor (the classic ERC-4626 inflation-attack surface); a virtual-shares/virtual-assets offset applied consistently in both directions, or a minimum initial deposit whose shares are minted to the program, is the standard mitigation. Separately, it is worth gating `process_update_reward` so it cannot be invoked by anyone on a vault with no outstanding shares, since in that configuration there is no holder for the reward to accrue to.
content.impact: Permanent denial of service on an affected vault plus stranded funds. Once a vault is in the `shares == 0 && assets > 0` state, every call to `process_deposit_with_fee` reverts at `mint_shares`'s `require_gt!(amt, 0)` guard for any deposit amount, and `process_deposit_with_fee_exact` reverts with MathOverflow via division by a zero share supply. No shares exist that could be burned, so the assets held by the vault's asset PDA — the attacker's donation and anything else accrued — are unrecoverable through normal vault operations. The vault is effectively dead and must be redeployed.
content.attack_path:
1. A vault is created and has not yet received its first deposit, so `vault.shares == 0` and `vault.assets == 0`.
2. The attacker transfers one asset token directly into the vault's asset PDA.
3. The attacker calls the permissionless `process_update_reward`. `vault_update_reward` calls `add_token(reward)`, increasing `vault.assets` while minting no shares, leaving `shares == 0 && assets > 0`.
4. Any honest user now calls `process_deposit_with_fee` with any `amount > 0` (the counterexample uses `amount = 2^64 - 1`, `assets = 2^64 - 1`, `fee_bps = 9999`). `convert_assets_to_shares` evaluates `mul_div_floor(net, 0, assets) = 0`, and `mint_shares(0)` fails `require_gt!(amt, 0)` — the call returns `Err` (`o = 0` in the trace).
5. `process_deposit_with_fee_exact` on the same state fails with MathOverflow because `convert_shares_to_assets` divides by `num_shares() == 0`.
6. No shares exist to burn, so the donated assets cannot be withdrawn and the vault is permanently unusable.
content.assumptions_and_uncertainties: The trace directly evidences the failure of `vault_deposit_assets_with_fee`'s accounting core only. The claim that the `_exact` variant is dead on the same state (via `convert_shares_to_assets` dividing by `num_shares() == 0`) and the claim that `process_update_reward` / `vault_update_reward` can create the `shares == 0 && assets > 0` state permissionlessly both follow from reading the source as reported in the analysis, not from this counterexample. The rule exercises the pure `&mut Vault` transition and does not touch handler account plumbing, so the end-to-end handler-level reachability assumes the handlers call this accounting core without an earlier guard that would reject the state; the analysis indicates they do. Severity assumes vaults can exist in a pre-first-deposit state exposed to the permissionless reward-update path.

provenance.risk_reasoning: The counterexample lies inside the property's plain domain (positive assets, legal fee_bps, positive amount) and shows the deposit core returning Err regardless of amount, so the break is unconditional on that pre-state. The pre-state itself is reachable by any unprivileged actor on a freshly created vault at the cost of one asset token plus a call to the permissionless `process_update_reward`, and the result — all deposits permanently reverting with no way to burn shares and recover the assets — is a permanent freeze of the vault and its balance.

findings.title: DepositWithFeeContext never re-derives the vault's shares-mint (or vault-assets) PDA, accepting attacker-substituted mint and asset accounts

content.summary: `DepositWithFeeContext::validate` validates `shares_mint` and `vault_assets_account` only by comparing them to fields read out of the caller-supplied `Vault` account, and never re-derives the canonical PDAs the way `DepositContext::validate` does via `VaultSharesMint::check_vault`. The Prover produced a concrete execution in which `load` returns `Ok` for a shares-mint account that is not the program-derived address, so the fee-deposit handlers go on to sign a `mint_to` CPI with a bump taken from unverified vault state against a substituted mint.
content.description:
`rule_fee_deposit_does_not_rederive_shares_mint_pda` sets up a nondeterministic account array and a nondeterministic `Vault` that is self-consistent with the accounts passed (`v.shares_mint = *accounts[4].key`, `v.assets_mint = *accounts[3].key`, `v.vault_assets_account = *accounts[1].key`, `v.fee_token_account = *accounts[2].key`), concedes everything the property does not contest — `accounts[0].owner == &crate::ID`, exact `Vault` data length, `v.assets_mint != v.shares_mint`, a real signer, the real SPL Token program id, no asset-account aliasing — and then assumes the supplied `accounts[4].key` is *not* the address returned by the program's own `create_vault_shares_mint_address(accounts[0].key, &v)`. It asserts `DepositWithFeeContext::load(..).is_err()`.

The Prover refuted it. The trace enters only `DepositWithFeeContext::load`, draws all six vault scalars as `0` (both bumps, `shares`, `assets`, `fee_bps`, `fee_amount`), and logs `ie: '0'` — i.e. `load` returned `Ok` — before the assertion at `fee_based_deposits.rs:611` fails. Nothing exotic was needed: none of those scalars is consulted on the validation path, so a zeroed vault buffer with a zero `vault_shares_mint_bump` is accepted just the same.

The root cause is visible in the source. In `programs/vault/src/loaders/vault_with_fee_loaders.rs`, both PDA-bearing slots are declared as bare `AccountInfo<'info>` and are filled in `load` with `next_account_info(iter)?.clone()`. `validate` then performs exactly four comparisons — `vault.assets_mint == assets_mint.key`, `vault.shares_mint == shares_mint.key`, `vault.vault_assets_account == vault_assets_account.key`, `vault.fee_token_account == vault_fee_account.key` — and returns `Ok(self)`. There is no call to `create_vault_shares_mint_address`, no `VaultSharesMint::check_vault`, and no use of the `VaultSharesMint`/`VaultAssetsAccount` wrapper types anywhere on this path. `DepositContext::validate` in `vault_loaders.rs` types the same slot as `VaultSharesMint<'info>` and, after the identical `require_eq!`, calls `self.shares_mint.check_vault(self.vault_info.as_ref().key, &vault)?`, re-deriving `[SHARES_MINT, vault_pk, bump]` under `crate::ID`. The fee path simply omits that step for both PDA slots.

Consequently `require_eq!(&vault.shares_mint, self.shares_mint.key, ..)` constrains nothing: both sides originate from caller-supplied input. The only gate before those comparisons is `VaultInfo::try_from` → `VaultInfo::validate` → `Vault::validate`, which enforces only `require_ne!(assets_mint, shares_mint)` — a condition every honest vault satisfies.

Downstream (a source-level consequence, not something this trace executes), both `process_deposit_with_fee` and `process_deposit_with_fee_exact` read `vault_info.get()?.vault_shares_mint_bump` and pass `crate::vault_shares_mint_seeds_with_bump!(vault_info.as_ref().key, shares_mint_bump)` into `spl_mint_shares` against the unverified `shares_mint`, and similarly route the user's assets into the unverified `vault_assets_account` via `spl_transfer_assets_from_user`.

Two halves of the evidence, stated explicitly: the counterexample proves `load` returns `Ok` on an account set constrained only by the vault's own self-reported fields; the fact that there is no derivation check at all to consult comes from reading `DepositWithFeeContext::validate`. The second half matters because the Solana Prover summarizes `Pubkey::create_program_address`, so the `expected` address the rule obtained is an unconstrained pubkey; read purely as a Prover artifact the rule would also fail against a program that *did* re-derive. The source reading settles the point that no such re-derivation exists. The same caveat attaches to the companion vault-assets-account rule, whose verdict is not covered here.

A related trust-root gap compounds this: even with re-derivation added, the bump is read out of the `Vault` account, and `impl TryFrom<&AccountInfo> for VaultInfo` does not enforce `info.owner == &crate::ID` or check a discriminator before `bytemuck::from_bytes` interprets the data (its `// owned by vault program` / `// has discriminant` comments are unimplemented intentions). `VaultInfo::get` also slices `data[0..size_of::<Vault>()]` unconditionally and would panic on a short account.
content.impact: Deposited assets can be routed to an account the attacker controls rather than the canonical vault assets PDA, and shares can be issued from a substituted mint, with the `mint_to` CPI signed using a bump read from unverified vault state. This breaks the core guarantee that deposit handlers reject non-canonical vault asset/mint accounts and puts depositor funds and share accounting at risk.
content.attack_path:
1. Attacker constructs a `Vault` account buffer (or supplies one it controls) whose `shares_mint` field holds the key of an attacker-chosen mint, whose `vault_assets_account` field holds an attacker-chosen token account, and with arbitrary (e.g. zero) `vault_shares_mint_bump` / `vault_assets_account_bump` — all balance and fee scalars may be zero.
2. Attacker calls `process_deposit_with_fee` (or `..._exact`) passing that vault account at index 0, the substituted token account at index 1, and the substituted mint at index 4.
3. `DepositWithFeeContext::load` → `validate` compares each supplied key only against the matching field in that same vault buffer; all four `require_eq!` checks pass, and `Vault::validate`'s single `assets_mint != shares_mint` check is satisfied. `load` returns `Ok` (the counterexample's `ie: '0'`).
4. The handler transfers the user's assets into the substituted `vault_assets_account` and signs the `mint_to` CPI with `vault_shares_mint_seeds_with_bump!(vault_pk, shares_mint_bump)` where the bump came from the same unverified vault state, issuing shares from the substituted mint.
content.assumptions_and_uncertainties: The counterexample itself establishes only that `DepositWithFeeContext::load` returns `Ok` for a shares-mint account that is not the canonically derived PDA; the downstream exploitation (the `mint_to`/transfer CPIs signed with the unverified bump) is read from `process_deposit_with_fee` / `process_deposit_with_fee_exact`, not exhibited by this trace. Because the Prover summarizes `Pubkey::create_program_address`, the rule's `expected` address is unconstrained, so the trace alone cannot distinguish a missing check from an independent derivation — the claim that no derivation exists rests on direct reading of `DepositWithFeeContext::validate`, which contains no `check_vault` or `create_vault_shares_mint_address` call. The vault-assets-account half of the property is asserted from the same source reading; its companion rule's verdict was not provided. Full exploitability also depends on how readily an attacker can supply a `Vault` account with chosen field values, which the missing owner/discriminator checks in `VaultInfo::try_from` make materially easier.

provenance.risk_reasoning: The counterexample required no exotic state — all vault scalars were zero and every conceded assumption (program-owned vault, correct data length, real signer, real token program) is what an honest call looks like — so `load` accepts a substituted mint on the ordinary fee-deposit path, reachable by any caller who can present a vault buffer whose self-reported fields name the substituted accounts; the practical bar is obtaining/controlling such a vault account, which is made easier by the missing owner and discriminator checks in `VaultInfo::try_from`. Impact is high because the result is misrouted deposits and shares minted from an attacker-chosen mint under a program-signed CPI.

findings.title: DepositWithFeeContext never re-derives the vault PDAs, so a self-consistent forged Vault lets an attacker substitute the vault asset account and shares mint

content.summary: `DepositWithFeeContext::validate` validates `vault_assets_account` and `shares_mint` only by comparing them against fields read out of the caller-supplied `Vault` buffer, and never re-derives the canonical PDAs the way `DepositContext::validate` does via `check_vault`. The Certora Prover produced a concrete execution in which `load` returns `Ok` for an account set whose asset account is not the program address derived from `[VAULT_ASSETS, vault_info.key, vault.vault_assets_account_bump]`, so fee deposits can be routed through a substituted token account and shares minted with an attacker-chosen bump.
content.description:
The rule `rule_fee_deposit_does_not_rederive_vault_assets_pda` asserts that `DepositWithFeeContext::load(&accounts[0..9])` must return an error whenever the supplied `accounts[1].key` (the vault assets account slot) differs from the program address derived by `crate::state::create_vault_assets_account_address(accounts[0].key, &vault)`. The harness conceded everything the property does not contest: `accounts[0].owner == &crate::ID` (a genuinely program-owned vault account), `accounts[0].data_len() == size_of::<Vault>()`, `v.assets_mint != v.shares_mint`, `accounts[6].is_signer`, `accounts[8].key == spl_token::id()`, and no aliasing between vault and user asset accounts. It also made the vault self-consistent with the passed accounts — exactly what an attacker who controls the `Vault` bytes would do — by setting `v.vault_assets_account = *accounts[1].key`, `v.assets_mint = *accounts[3].key`, `v.shares_mint = *accounts[4].key`, `v.fee_token_account = *accounts[2].key`.

The Prover found a concrete model satisfying all of these assumptions in which `load` nevertheless returned `Ok` (`ie: '0'`, assertion at `fee_based_deposits.rs:589` failed). The nondeterministic scalars were all drawn as zero (`vault_shares_mint_bump`, `vault_assets_account_bump`, `shares`, `assets`, `fee_bps`, `fee_amount`), confirming the acceptance requires nothing exotic — none of those values is consulted on the validation path at all.

Reading the implementation confirms the mechanism. In `programs/vault/src/loaders/vault_with_fee_loaders.rs`, `DepositWithFeeContext` declares both PDA-bearing slots as bare `AccountInfo<'info>` and `load` fills them with `next_account_info(iter)?.clone()`. `validate` then performs only four equality checks — `vault.assets_mint == assets_mint.key`, `vault.shares_mint == shares_mint.key`, `vault.vault_assets_account == vault_assets_account.key`, `vault.fee_token_account == vault_fee_account.key` — and returns `Ok(self)`. There is no call to `create_vault_assets_account_address`, no `VaultAssetsAccount::check_vault`, and no use of the checked wrapper types anywhere on this path. By contrast, `DepositContext::validate` in `vault_loaders.rs` types the same slot as `VaultAssetsAccount<'info>` and, after the identical `require_eq!`, calls `self.vault_assets_account.check_vault(self.vault_info.as_ref().key, &vault)?`, re-deriving `[VAULT_ASSETS, vault_pk, bump]` under `crate::ID`. The fee-deposit context simply omits that step.

Because both sides of `require_eq!(&vault.vault_assets_account, self.vault_assets_account.key, ..)` originate from caller-supplied inputs, the comparison constrains nothing about the real world. The only gate standing before it is `VaultInfo::try_from` → `VaultInfo::validate` → `Vault::validate`, which enforces only `require_ne!(assets_mint, shares_mint)` — a condition every honest vault satisfies. Notably, `VaultInfo::try_from` does not enforce `info.owner == &crate::ID` or any discriminator check (the `// owned by vault program` and `// has discriminant` comments are unimplemented intentions), so in practice the `Vault` bytes — including the bumps — are attacker-controllable, though the rule did not even need to exploit that, having granted program ownership outright.

Downstream of the accepted context, `process_deposit_with_fee` transfers the net deposit via `spl_transfer_assets_from_user` into whatever account occupies slot 1 while crediting `vault.assets` as if the funds had reached the real vault PDA, and `spl_mint_shares` signs with `vault_shares_mint_seeds_with_bump!(vault_info.key, vault.vault_shares_mint_bump)` — a bump read from the same unverified buffer. The same omission applies to the shares-mint slot.

Evidential caveat to carry with this finding: the Solana Prover summarizes `Pubkey::create_program_address`, so the `expected` address the rule obtained is an unconstrained pubkey. Read purely as a Prover artifact, the witness would also arise against a program that did re-derive and compare. The trace is therefore sound evidence for one half of the claim — that `load` returns `Ok` on an account set constrained only by the vault's own self-reported fields — while the source itself supplies the other half: `DepositWithFeeContext::validate` contains no derivation call to consult.
content.impact: An attacker can call the fee-deposit handlers with a substituted `vault_assets_account` (and likewise a substituted `shares_mint`) that is not the canonical program-derived address. The deposited assets are transferred into an account the attacker controls while `vault.assets` is credited as though the real vault PDA received them, and shares are minted under a bump taken from unverified vault state. This desynchronizes vault accounting from actual holdings and routes user deposits to an unauthorized account, enabling theft of deposited funds and leaving the vault unable to honor later redemptions.
content.attack_path:
1. Prepare a `Vault` account of the correct size whose `vault_assets_account` field names an attacker-controlled token account (and whose `shares_mint`/bump fields are chosen by the attacker), satisfying the only enforced invariant `assets_mint != shares_mint`.
2. Invoke a fee-deposit instruction, passing that vault account in slot 0 and the attacker-controlled token account in slot 1 (and a substituted mint in slot 4).
3. `DepositWithFeeContext::load` → `validate` compares `vault.vault_assets_account` against `accounts[1].key` — both attacker-supplied and equal by construction — and performs no PDA re-derivation, so it returns `Ok`.
4. `process_deposit_with_fee` transfers the net deposit via `spl_transfer_assets_from_user` into the substituted account while incrementing `vault.assets`, and `spl_mint_shares` signs with `vault.vault_shares_mint_bump` read from the unverified buffer.
content.assumptions_and_uncertainties: The counterexample directly establishes only that `DepositWithFeeContext::load` accepts an account set whose asset account is constrained solely by the vault's self-reported field; the downstream exploitation chain (misrouted `spl_transfer_assets_from_user` transfer and `spl_mint_shares` signing with an unverified bump) is a source-level inference from the two handlers, not something the trace exhibits. Because the Prover summarizes `Pubkey::create_program_address`, the derived `expected` address in the harness is unconstrained, so the witness alone does not distinguish a re-deriving program from a non-re-deriving one — the absence of any `check_vault` / `create_vault_assets_account_address` call in `DepositWithFeeContext::validate`, versus its presence in `DepositContext::validate`, is what closes that gap. Full attacker control of the `Vault` bytes additionally depends on the missing owner and discriminator checks in `VaultInfo::try_from`; the rule granted program ownership and still saw acceptance, so the loader defect stands independently, but the practical severity is compounded by that second gap. The fix must add `check_vault` for both the assets account and the shares mint and simultaneously enforce the owner/discriminator/data-length checks in `VaultInfo`, since re-derivation is only as trustworthy as the bump it reads.

provenance.risk_reasoning: The counterexample required no special values — all nondeterministic scalars were zero and every granted assumption (program-owned vault, distinct mints, signer, SPL token program) is what an honest caller already satisfies — so any unprivileged caller can supply a self-consistent vault plus a substituted asset account. Acceptance leads directly to assets being transferred to an attacker-named account while the vault's `assets` counter is credited, and to `mint_to` being signed with an unverified bump, i.e. direct loss of deposited funds and broken solvency.

findings.title: `vault_deposit_assets_with_fee_exact` never commits the deposit to vault state, permanently stranding depositor assets

content.summary: The exact fee-deposit accounting core `vault_deposit_assets_with_fee_exact` computes a `VaultEffect` but, unlike both of its sibling operations, never calls `vault.mint_shares(...)` or `vault.add_token(...)`. `process_deposit_with_fee_exact` nevertheless performs all three CPIs — pulling the user's assets in and minting share tokens — while `vault.shares` and `vault.assets` stay unchanged, so the subsequent `vault_redeem_shares` underflows in `burn_shares` and the deposited assets can never be withdrawn.
content.description:
The rule `rule_fee_deposit_shares_are_redeemable_without_profit_exact` drives the program's own accounting core over a `&mut Vault`: it assumes a solvent pre-state, calls `crate::operations::vault_deposit_assets_with_fee_exact(&mut v, amount)`, assumes it returned `Ok` with `shares_to_user = s > 0`, and then requires that `crate::operations::vault_redeem_shares(&mut v, s)` succeeds and pays out at most `assets_to_vault = n`.

The counterexample is an entirely ordinary state — a freshly initialised vault:

- pre-state `shares = 0`, `assets = 0` (solvency `0 <= 0` holds trivially)
- `fee_bps = 0`
- `amount = 1924`

The deposit returns `Ok` with `shares_to_user = 1924`, `assets_to_vault = 1924`, `assets_to_fee = 0`. Every step is reproducible by hand: `fee_bps.apply(1924)` at a zero rate gives `net = 1924, fee = 0`; `convert_assets_to_shares(1924)` takes the `num_shares() == num_assets()` shortcut (`0 == 0`) and returns `1924`; `convert_shares_to_assets(1924)` does the same; the recomputed fee is again `0`.

The assertion that fired at `fee_based_deposits.rs:858` is `cvlr_assert!(ok2)` — the "can the position be unwound at all" half of the property, not the `payout <= n` half. The trace shows `o2 = 0`, i.e. `vault_redeem_shares` returned `Err`; the logged `payout = 0` is merely the `unwrap_or_default()` filler, not a computed payout. This is therefore not a rounding subtlety: the redeem flatly failed.

Root cause: in `programs/vault/src/operations/vault_exact_deposit_operations.rs`, `vault_deposit_assets_with_fee_exact` takes `&mut Vault` and never writes to it. Its body computes the fee rate, the provisional gross/net split, `shares_to_user = vault.convert_assets_to_shares(gross.net_amount)?`, `assets_to_vault = vault.convert_shares_to_assets(shares_to_user)?` and the recomputed `actual_gross`, then constructs and returns the `VaultEffect`. There is no `vault.mint_shares(shares_to_user)?` and no `vault.add_token(assets_to_vault)?`. The omission is unambiguous when compared with its siblings: `vault_deposit_assets_with_fee` in `vault_fee_operations.rs` calls both before returning its effect, and `vault_deposit_assets_exact`, in the same file as the defective function, calls both as well. The fee-plus-exact variant reads like a copy of `vault_deposit_assets_exact` with the fee computation spliced in and the two mutating lines dropped.

The handler consequence: `process_deposit_with_fee_exact` takes that effect record and unconditionally issues three CPIs — transfer `assets_to_vault` from the user into `vault_assets_account`, transfer `assets_to_fee` into the fee account, and `mint_to` `shares_to_user` share tokens to the user — while the vault's recorded `shares` and `assets` remain at their pre-call values. In the witness the depositor hands over 1924 asset tokens and receives 1924 newly minted share tokens, yet the vault's books still read `shares = 0, assets = 0`. A subsequent `vault_redeem_shares(&mut v, 1924)` calls `burn_shares(1924)` against a recorded supply of `0`; the `checked_sub` returns `None` and the operation fails with `MathOverflow`.
